chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Find.description:
FindingAssessment is what hardening did about a finding, derived by the
pipeline from the edits it applied rather than from model output.

 - FINDING_ASSESSMENT_UNSPECIFIED: FINDING_ASSESSMENT_UNSPECIFIED: not assessed, as for an introduced
finding or a report written before assessments existed.
 - FINDING_ASSESSMENT_FIXED: FINDING_ASSESSMENT_FIXED: an applied edit targeted the finding and it
closed.
 - FINDING_ASSESSMENT_RETAINED: FINDING_ASSESSMENT_RETAINED: hardening chose to keep the flagged content.
 - FINDING_ASSESSMENT_NOT_ADDRESSED: FINDING_ASSESSMENT_NOT_ADDRESSED: no applied edit targeted the finding.
FindingSeverity is the normalized CGSVT level, most severe first.

FindingStatus is a finding's outcome across hardening.

 - FINDING_STATUS_CLOSED: FINDING_STATUS_CLOSED: present before hardening, gone after.
 - FINDING_STATUS_OPEN: FINDING_STATUS_OPEN: present before and after hardening.
 - FINDING_STATUS_INTRODUCED: FINDING_STATUS_INTRODUCED: present only after hardening.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Hard.description:
HardenSkillRequest names a skill artifact already uploaded to uploads.cgr.dev
and the group to harden it into. The caller supplies components, not a ref:
the server builds the digest-pinned source ref
uploads.cgr.dev/<group>/<skill_name>@sha256:<content_digest> from the fields
below — the host is a server constant, never caller input, so a caller can
never point the harden pipeline at an arbitrary registry. On success the
hardened result is published to a per-user path,
skills.cgr.dev/<group>/users/<actor>/<skill_name> (the user-less
skills.cgr.dev/<group>/<skill_name> path is reserved for promotion).

Every source normalizes to an uploads.cgr.dev artifact before harden: customer
uploads (chainctl skills push), public Chainguard skills, and Chainguard's
internal skills are all pushed to uploads.cgr.dev by the pipeline's ingest
phase — the only stage that fetches upstream content. So this endpoint only
ever names an uploads artifact by digest; there is no remote/git source on
this surface.

contentDigest.description:
content_digest is the sha256 digest of the uploaded artifact, as
"sha256:<64-hex>". It is the content dimension of the source ref: the server
builds the pinned OCI ref uploads.cgr.dev/<group>/<skill_name>@<content_digest>
(host fixed server-side) and the pipeline pulls the artifact by it. The API
never carries file bytes — the --folder and --digest client modes both
resolve to this digest. The server validates the format and rejects anything
that is not a well-formed sha256 digest.

group.description:
group is the target group (org UIDP) the skill is hardened into. It is
authorized against the caller (the IAM scope for CAP_SKILLS_HARDEN_WRITE),
never derived from identity. The hardened skill lands under a per-user path,
skills.cgr.dev/<group>/users/<actor>/<skill_name>; the user-less
skills.cgr.dev/<group>/<skill_name> path is reserved for promotion.

retryOf.description:
retry_of is the full name of a failed operation to retry. The operation
must belong to this caller and match group, skill_name and content_digest.
It is preserved, and a new operation tracks the retry. Repeating the same
retry_of returns the same retry operation, including its terminal result.
To retry again, name that failed retry operation. Empty retains ordinary
content-addressed submission. Successful, pending or cancelled jobs cannot
be retried.

skillName.description:
skill_name is the skill's catalog name (from --name or SKILL.md
frontmatter). It is the path the hardened skill takes under the group's
skills folder.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Hard.description: HardeningFinding is one CGSVT finding: a distinct (group, subtype, file).

assessment.description:
assessment is what hardening did about the finding. UNSPECIFIED for
introduced findings and on reports written before the field existed.

detectorCount.description: detector_count is the number of distinct scanners that raised it.

operationalId.description: operational_id is the finding's stable identity across hardening.

rationaleId.description:
rationale_id names the APPROVED Rationale that explains the assessment;
empty when none applies. Read the text with ListRationales.

sources.description: sources are in display order: sources[0] names the finding.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Hard.description: Source is one scanner check that raised the finding.

name.description:
name is the check's display name; empty when the taxonomy does not
catalogue the rule.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Hard.description: HardeningReport is the hardening result for one skill version.

digest.description: digest is the hardened artifact digest the report describes.

passed.description: passed is true when the version cleared the hardening gate.

scannerRuns.description:
scanner_runs are the scanners evaluated for this version and how each
ended, so a version with no findings can be told apart from one whose
scanner did not finish. Empty on reports written before the field existed.

summary.description:
summary is the pipeline's templated prose summary of the result. Empty on
reports written before the field existed.

tagId.description: tag_id is the registry tag UIDP of the skill version.

taxonomyVersion.description: taxonomy_version is the CGSVT version the findings are classified under.

unroutedEntries.description:
unrouted are scanner labels CGSVT does not classify, kept so a high or
critical unknown is still counted.

versionSha.description: version_sha is the upstream commit the version was built from.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Hard.description: ScannerRun is one scanner's outcome in one evaluation.

Phase is the skill the scanner evaluated, matching before and after.

 - PHASE_BEFORE: PHASE_BEFORE is the submitted skill, before hardening.
 - PHASE_AFTER: PHASE_AFTER is the hardened skill.

- STATUS_FAILED: STATUS_FAILED means the scanner did not finish: its findings are
missing from the report, not zero.
 - STATUS_SKIPPED: STATUS_SKIPPED means the scanner is not enabled in this environment,
so it did not scan the skill.

digest.description: digest is the digest of the report the page was read from.

totalSize.description: total_size is the number of findings matching the filter.

total_size counts the stored reports the filter matches, including any
whose tag has since moved.
total_size is the number of entries matching the filter.

paths.description: paths are the files' relative paths, sorted.

items.description: items are one page of distinct sources in scope, ordered by slug.

nextPageToken.description: Token for the next page, empty when there are no more results.
next_page_token is the token for the next page (empty if no more pages).

totalCount.description: total_count is the total number of skills matching the filter.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Rati.description:
Rationale is one reviewed rationale catalog entry. Its text is generic: it
names no skill, path or command, so one entry serves many findings.

assessments.description: assessments are the finding assessments the entry can explain.

deprecated.description:
deprecated entries are no longer chosen for new findings but still
explain the findings that reference them.

groupIds.description:
group_ids are the CGSVT groups the entry is written for, e.g. "CGSVT-08";
empty when it applies to any group.

id.description: id is the entry's stable identity, referenced by findings.

reviewer.description:
reviewer is who approved or rejected the entry; empty for an entry
created APPROVED or not yet reviewed. Only catalog writers see it.

state.description:
state is required to create an entry (PENDING or APPROVED) and is changed
only by ReviewRationale. On an update it is left unset or matches the
stored state.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Rati.description:
RationaleState is where a rationale catalog entry is in review. Only
APPROVED entries can be cited by findings or listed publicly.

 - RATIONALE_STATE_PENDING: RATIONALE_STATE_PENDING: proposed, awaiting review.
 - RATIONALE_STATE_APPROVED: RATIONALE_STATE_APPROVED: reviewed and citable.
 - RATIONALE_STATE_REJECTED: RATIONALE_STATE_REJECTED: reviewed and refused; the id is never reused.

nextPageToken.description: next_page_token is the token for the next page (empty if no more pages).

totalCount.description: total_count is the total number of skills matching the query.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Seve.description: SeverityCounts tallies findings by level; critical is never folded into high.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Skil.description:
Skill is one hardened skill in the catalog. Content (SKILL.md + references)
lives in the OCI registry; this record carries the catalog metadata the
registry does not (description, license, category). Read-only over the public
API — populated internally at publish time.

category.description: category groups the skill in the catalog, if declared.

createTime.description: create_time is when the skill was first recorded.

description.description: description is a human-readable one-line summary.

downloads.description: downloads is the accumulated download/pull count for the skill.

hardened.description:
hardened is true when any of the skill's versions passed evaluation. Backs
the "Hardened" chip on the catalog directory page.

id.description: id, the skill's UIDP under the owning Group.

keywords.description:
keywords are free-form tags associated with the skill. Field 6 is reclaimed
from the removed digest field: digest = 6 (string) shipped in SDK
v0.1.159-v0.1.165, but the catalog was never populated or consumed in that
window, so the slot is reused for keywords (repeated string).

license.description: license is the skill's SPDX license identifier, if declared.

name.description: name is the skill's normalized short catalog name, e.g. "academy-guide".

source.description: source is the organization that published the skill (e.g. "anthropics").

sourceBrowseUrl.description:
source_browse_url links to the skill's folder upstream at its tracked
branch; it equals source_repo_url for a whole-repository skill.

sourcePath.description:
source_path is the skill's folder within source_repo_url, e.g.
"skills/academy-guide"; empty when the skill is the whole repository.

sourceRepoUrl.description:
source_repo_url is the browsable upstream repository the skill was
ingested from, e.g. "https://github.com/agentspace-so/agent-skills"; empty
when unknown. Public because only public auto-ingested skills are in the
catalog.

stars.description: stars is the accumulated count of stars (favorites) for the skill.

updateTime.description: update_time is when the skill was last updated.

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Skil.description: SkillFile is one file from a skill artifact.

group.description:
group is the owning group UIDP; the IAM scope. The operation cancelled is
harden/{group}/{job_id}.

source.description:
source is the slug to pass back as the ListSkills / SearchSkills `source`
filter, e.g. "anthropics".

chainguard.platform.skills.v1alpha1.Taxo.description: Taxonomy is one CGSVT version's display metadata.

unifiedSha256.description:

make a version immutable.

google.longrunning.Operation.description:
This resource represents a long-running operation that is the result of a
network API call.

done.description:
If the value is `false`, it means the operation is still in progress.
If `true`, the operation is completed, and either `error` or `response` is
available.

error.description: The error result of the operation in case of failure or cancellation.

metadata.description:
Service-specific metadata associated with the operation.  It typically
contains progress information and common metadata such as create time.
Some services might not provide such metadata.  Any method that returns a
long-running operation should document the metadata type, if any.

name.description:
The server-assigned name, which is only unique within the same service that
originally returns it. If you use the default HTTP mapping, the
`name` should be a resource name ending with `operations/{unique_id}`.

response.description:
The normal, successful response of the operation.  If the original
method returns no data on success, such as `Delete`, the response is
`google.protobuf.Empty`.  If the original method is standard
`Get`/`Create`/`Update`, the response should be the resource.  For other
methods, the response should have the type `XxxResponse`, where `Xxx`
is the original method name.  For example, if the original method name
is `TakeSnapshot()`, the inferred response type is
`TakeSnapshotResponse`.

tags.description:
Skills is the catalog surface for hardened Chainguard skills. Its customer-
facing side is a read API (ListSkills) — the shared backend consumed by the
cgr-skills MCP, chainctl, and the community UI (one backend, many front doors,
mirroring the registry ListRepos/ListTags endpoints). It also carries the
publish-time writes (UpdateSkill/DeleteSkill), which are internal_only and
hidden from the tool surface. Skill content is pulled from the OCI registry
(skills.cgr.dev); this API serves the catalog metadata (name, description,
category) the registry does not carry.

A skill is a registry Repo, so versions, digests, and content come from the
registry API (ListRepos/ListTags/GetTag + OCI). Ranked catalog search is
SearchSkills.
tags.name: Skills

tags.description:
SkillsHarden is the customer-facing on-demand skill-harden API. A caller
submits a skill artifact — already uploaded to uploads.cgr.dev — targeted at
a group, and receives a long-running Operation to track the harden pipeline.
It is the API-driven sibling of the synchronous `chainctl skills harden` MVP
and the registry-push-triggered reconciler, and the one path that lets a
caller submit a specific skill on demand and get a handle to track it.
tags.name: SkillsHarden

tags.description:
SkillsHardeningReports serves the hardening result for a skill version: the
before/after severity counts and the findings, classified by the Chainguard
Skill Vulnerability Taxonomy (CGSVT). A skill version is a registry tag, so
reports are keyed by the tag's UIDP. The writes are internal_only and hidden
from the tool surface; the skills pipeline is their only caller.
tags.name: SkillsHardeningReports
